name: PVInstance
simple: PVInstance is the family name for things that have a place in the 3D world, mainly parts and models. You never make one directly. Its job is to give parts and models two super useful tools: `GetPivot` (where is it?) and `PivotTo` (move it there).
analogy: Think of a pivot like the handle on a suitcase. Wherever you carry the handle, the whole suitcase comes along. `PivotTo` moves the handle, and everything attached moves with it, keeping the same shape.
whenToUse: Move a whole Model (like a car or a house) to a new spot with `PivotTo`.
Teleport a player's character by calling `PivotTo` on the character model.
Find out where a model or part is (and which way it faces) with `GetPivot`.
where: Built into every BasePart (Part, MeshPart, and so on) and every Model. Works in both Scripts (server) and LocalScripts (client).

terms.pivot: The handle point of a part or model. It has a position and a facing direction. For a plain part it is at the very center unless you change `PivotOffset`.
terms.CFrame: Short for coordinate frame. One value that holds BOTH a position (where) and a rotation (which way it faces).
terms.Model: A container that groups several parts into one object, like a car made of wheels, seats, and a body.
terms.stud: Roblox's unit of distance. A default Part is 4 studs long, 1 stud tall, and 2 studs wide.
terms.world space: Positions measured from the center of the whole map, the point (0, 0, 0).
terms.abstract class: A family name that groups related classes. You cannot create one with `Instance.new`; you create one of its members instead.
terms.radians: Another way to measure turning. A full circle is about 6.28 radians instead of 360 degrees. `math.rad(90)` converts 90 degrees to radians.

examples.title: Teleport a player when they touch a pad
examples.place: Script inside a Part named TeleportPad in Workspace
examples.code:
local pad = script.Parent
local destination = CFrame.new(0, 50, 0) -- 50 studs above the center of the map

pad.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
	local character = hit.Parent
	local humanoid = character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	if humanoid then
		-- Move the WHOLE character model, keeping its body parts together
		character:PivotTo(destination)
	end
end)
explain: When something touches the pad, `hit` is the body part that touched it, and `hit.Parent` is the character model.
We check for a Humanoid so we only teleport characters, not random parts.
`PivotTo` moves the character's pivot to (0, 50, 0). Every body part moves by the same amount, so the character stays in one piece.

examples.title: Slide a model 10 studs to the right
examples.code:
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")
local house = Workspace:WaitForChild("House") -- a Model

local current = house:GetPivot()            -- where it is now
print(current.Position)                       -- e.g. 20, 0, 5

-- Add an offset of (10, 0, 0): 10 studs along the world X axis
house:PivotTo(current + Vector3.new(10, 0, 0))
print(house:GetPivot().Position)              -- 30, 0, 5
explain: `GetPivot()` gives the model's current CFrame (position + rotation).
Adding a Vector3 to a CFrame moves it without turning it. A pivot at (20, 0, 5) plus (10, 0, 0) lands at (30, 0, 5).
`PivotTo` moves the model there. Its rotation stays the same.

gotchas: To move a Model, use `PivotTo`. Do not set each part's Position one by one; the parts can get out of line.
Calling `PivotTo` on a part that is welded to others also moves those welded parts, because they are attached.
`PivotTo` does not fire the Position or Orientation changed events on the parts it moves, only the CFrame one.

PVInstance.Origin.simple: Studio-only. In the Properties window it shows as Origin Position and Origin Orientation: where the pivot is in the world. Changing it in Studio moves the whole object. Scripts cannot use it; use `GetPivot` and `PivotTo` instead.

PVInstance.Pivot Offset.simple: Studio-only. In the Properties window it shows as Pivot Position and Pivot Orientation: where the pivot sits compared to the object itself. Changing it moves just the handle, not the object. Scripts cannot use it here; on a part, use `BasePart.PivotOffset` instead.

PVInstance:GetPivot.simple: Gives you the pivot as a CFrame: where the object's handle point is in the world, and which way it faces. For a plain part this is the same as its CFrame.
PVInstance:GetPivot.example:
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")
local car = Workspace:WaitForChild("Car")
local pivot = car:GetPivot()
print("Car is at", pivot.Position)
print("Car is facing", pivot.LookVector)

PVInstance:PivotTo.simple: Moves (and turns) the object so its pivot ends up exactly at the CFrame you give. Everything inside a model moves along with it and keeps the same shape. This is the main way to move models from code.
PVInstance:PivotTo.example:
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")
local car = Workspace:WaitForChild("Car")
-- Put the car at (0, 5, 0), turned 90 degrees to the left
car:PivotTo(CFrame.new(0, 5, 0) * CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(90), 0))
PVInstance:PivotTo.gotcha: `CFrame.Angles` takes radians, not degrees. Use `math.rad(90)` to turn 90 degrees into radians.
